bihar_raw_news.title: PM Modi launches several development projects worth ₹34 470 crore in Vaishali - Newsonair
bihar_raw_news.content: News On AIR | November 21, 2026 9:15 PM PM Modi launches several development projects worth ₹34 470 crore in Vaishali; Reiterates commitment to build Bihar that is stronger, more prosperous & full of opportunities Strengthening Bihar’s development and connectivity, Prime Minister Narendra Modi today inaugurated the Nitish Setu in Vaishali. On the occasion, he also inaugurated and laid the foundation stones of development projects worth over 34,000 crore rupees. Addressing the gathering, the Prime Minister highlighted Bihar’s development journey, good governance and various welfare initiatives. The Prime Minister Narendra Modi was accorded a traditional welcome with a stole adorned with Bajjika artwork, flowers made of makhana, a garland of Aparajita flowers and bananas. Following the welcome, the Prime Minister dedicated the six-lane Nitish Setu, built across the River Ganga, to the people of Bihar. Stretching approximately 20 kilometres, the bridge connects Kachchi Dargah in Patna district with Bidupur in Vaishali district. With the inauguration of this bridge, traffic pressure on the Mahatma Gandhi Setu and JP Setu is expected to ease, while connectivity between North and South Bihar will become smoother. The Prime Minister said that the bridge has been named in honour of former Chief Minister Nitish Kumar. He described it as a symbol of his service and dedication to Bihar. Describing Nitish Setu as more than just a means of transportation, the Prime Minister said that the project would make people’s daily lives easier. He added that it would help local products reach larger markets and improve access to education and healthcare services. In his address, the Prime Minister invoked the blessings of Chhathi Maiya and said that Bihar was celebrating a festival of development. He recalled that three decades ago, the people of Bihar had chosen the path of hope and faith, and that under the leadership of Nitish Kumar, the state had gained renewed confidence in good governance. During the programme, the Prime Minister presented a total of 227 development projects to the state. These include the second 660-megawatt unit of the Buxar Thermal Power Project, along with several initiatives related to road construction, power distribution and transmission, irrigation, education, healthcare and urban development. The Prime Minister also flagged off 100 electric buses under the PM-e-Bus initiative and participated in the Griha Pravesh ceremony for more than 26 900 beneficiaries of the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana-Urban. These projects are expected to strengthen connectivity, expand energy and urban infrastructure, improve public services and give fresh momentum to Bihar’s economic development.

bihar_raw_news.title: PM Modi says Bihar has bridged its past - MillenniumPost
bihar_raw_news.content: Home > Big Story > PM Modi says Bihar has bridged its past; Dedicates Rs 34,000-cr projects, including Nitish Setu over Ganga Big Story PM Modi says Bihar has bridged its past; Dedicates Rs 34,000-cr projects, including Nitish Setu over Ganga BY MPost 22 Nov 2026 12:40 AM IST X MPost 22 Nov 2026 12:40 AM IST Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday took a swipe at previous governments in Bihar, saying the state was once associated with crime and scams but the NDA government has shifted the focus to development and action against criminals. Addressing a gathering, he highlighted Bihar’s progress under the double-engine government. PM Modi cited improvements in infrastructure investment and public welfare. Modi addressed a rally in Jafarpatti of Vaishali district, about 50 km from the state capital, where he dedicated to the nation projects worth more than Rs 34,000 crore, including a bridge over the Ganga. The 9.76-km-long Nitish Setu, a six-lane bridge over the Ganga, connecting Bidupur block in Vaishali district to Kachchi Dargah on the outskirts of Patna has been named ‘Nitish Setu’ after former state chief minister Nitish Kumar. He said Nitish Kumar gave up the post of chief minister in April to make way for a BJP-helmed government and the bridge was named, “as a mark of respect for his contributions to the state”. The bridge has been built at a cost of around Rs 4,280 crore. After its inauguration, Modi, accompanied by Governor Syed Ata Hasnain, Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary, Union Minister Chirag Paswan, and Deputy CM Vijay Kumar Choudhary, walked on the bridge for a few minutes. The PM also waved to the crowd with a ‘gamcha’. “The state has come a long way since the NDA took over. Earlier, only scams and crimes were talked about. Now Bihar makes news for investment proposals and action taken against those who indulge in any type of wrongdoing,” he said. Modi, who was speaking in an area falling under the Hajipur Lok Sabha constituency, represented by Union minister Chirag Paswan, also recalled the contributions of the latter’s late father Ram Vilas Paswan, who had represented the parliamentary seat several times. The PM also trained his guns at the Congress, accusing it of having “misled people with slogans of garibi hatao”, drawing a contrast with the NDA government at the Centre over the last 12 years during which “50 crore people have moved out of the clutches of poverty”. Major road projects that were inaugurated include the six-laning of the NH-19, the Chorma-Bairgania section of NH-227F and the Umagaon-Saharsa section of NH-327, among others, the officials said. The PM inaugurated the second unit (660 MW) of the 1,320 MW Buxar Thermal Power Project, along with electricity distribution and transmission infrastructure projects under the Energy Department. Other projects that were inaugurated during the day include restoration and strengthening of canals and embankments, a floating solar project at Phulwaria Dam in Nawada and sewerage infrastructure at Kahalgaon. The PM also inaugurated buildings and facilities

national_raw_news.content: Culture and Tourism Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat had a bilateral ministerial-level discussion with the Azerbaijani delegation on the sidelines of the SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum in New Delhi today. In a social media post, Mr Shekhawat said that during the meeting, their discussions focused on deepening India-Azerbaijan cultural cooperation, building on centuries-old historical connections, trade and people-to-people exchanges. He noted that the Ateshgah Fire Temple near Baku, with its inscriptions in Devanagari and Gurmukhi, stands as a remarkable testament to India-Azerbaijan shared historical links. They also explored avenues for collaboration in heritage conservation, manuscript digitisation, museum exchanges, academic research and the preservation of our shared cultural legacy. Mr Shekhawat reaffirmed that India looks forward to strengthening these civilisational bonds and building a deeper cultural partnership with Azerbaijan. The Minister also had a bilateral interaction with the Minister of Culture of Tajikistan, Sattoriyon Matlubakhon Amonzoda. In a social media post, Mr Shekhawat said that the discussions focused on taking cultural partnership forward through the preservation and digitisation of shared manuscripts, promotion of literary heritage, exchanges between artists and cultural institutions, and greater academic collaboration. He also noted that the recent inscription of Tajikistan’s Sumanak tradition on UNESCO’s Representative List of Intangible Cultural Heritage is another celebration of the rich cultural traditions that connect the region. The Minister said that both the countries share a civilisational bond that transcends geography, rooted in centuries of history, literature, language and cultural exchange.

national_raw_news.title: PM Modi inaugurates several development projects worth ₹34,470 crore in Bihar
national_raw_news.content: In a major infrastructure boost to Bihar, Prime Minister Narendra Modi today inaugurated and dedicated to the nation several development projects worth around 34,470 crore rupees in Vaishali. The projects cover several key sectors, including road connectivity, energy, urban infrastructure, education, healthcare, water resources and transport. The Prime Minister dedicated Nitish Setu, a six-lane bridge across the Ganga, to the nation. Built at a cost of around 4280 crore rupees, the 19.7-kilometre bridge connects Kachchi Dargah in Patna district with Bidupur in Vaishali. It is expected to ease traffic congestion on Mahatma Gandhi Setu and JP Setu, reduce travel time and strengthen connectivity between North and South Bihar. The Prime Minister inaugurated, worth over 15,600 crore rupees development projects including major road projects, the 660-megawatt second unit of the Buxar Thermal Power Project, electricity distribution and transmission works. He inaugurated infrastructure related to irrigation, education, healthcare and urban development. He also laid the foundation stone of projects worth around 14,450 crore rupees. These include the four-laning of the Sahebganj-Areraj-Bettiah section of National Highway-139W, a power evacuation project for the Pirpainti Super Thermal Power Project, and several urban water supply and sewerage projects. Other initiatives include canal modernisation, educational institutions, the IIT Patna Research Park and hostel, and emergency response infrastructure. The Prime Minister flagged off 100 PM-eBuses and participated in the Griha Pravesh ceremony for over 26, 900 beneficiaries under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana-Urban. The projects are expected to strengthen infrastructure, improve public services and accelerate economic development across Bihar.

national_raw_news.title: HM Amit Shah congratulates NCB, US DEA on Operation Monsoon Thunder
national_raw_news.content: Home Minister Amit Shah today congratulated the Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) and the United States Drug Enforcement Administration (US DEA) on the success of Operation Monsoon Thunder. In a social media post, Mr Shah said that the arrests made and seizures effected in India and the US under this campaign stand as a testament to the power of the India-US partnership in curbing the menace of drugs. He also highlighted that under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, India is firmly committed to ensuring that neither a gram of narcotics enters the country nor leaves for other countries. Meanwhile, US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor also hailed the India-U.S. partnership in cracking down on a transnational drug trafficking network under Operation Monsoon Thunder. In a social media post, Mr Gor said that India’s Narcotics Control Bureau, in close coordination with the US Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA), disrupted the network allegedly supplying illegal drugs to consumers across the United States and apprehended six individuals. Mr Gor thanked Home Minister Amit Shah for his leadership and described the action as an example of the India-US partnership. The Narcotics Control Bureau of India has successfully busted the Indian module of a transnational drug trafficking network facilitating the supply of psychotropic and opioid drugs within the United States in close coordination with the US DEA under Operation Monsoon Thunder. NCB said that the network operated through digital platforms, including Telegram and WhatsApp, with Google Sheets used for managing orders. The law enforcement agency informed that six individuals have been apprehended during the operation; approximately three thousand parcels involving nearly 500 thousand tablets were identified, which were shipped within the USA; data relating to over 59 thousand US subjects was shared with the US DEA, and two live consignments were intercepted by the US DEA. The agency said that the operation underscored the strength of India-US law enforcement cooperation and the commitment of both agencies to dismantling transnational drug trafficking networks. It further added that NCB India remains committed to combating drug trafficking through intelligence-led enforcement and strong international partnerships.

national_raw_news.title: 57th IFFI opens in Goa with 150 films from 86 countries, celebrating cinema without borders
national_raw_news.content: The 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) opened in Goa on Friday, with a spectacular inaugural ceremony at Dr. Shyama Prasad Mukherjee Stadium, bringing together filmmakers, film personalities and cinema enthusiasts from across the world. With more than 150 films from 86 countries, this year’s festival is being held under the theme ‘Stories Without Borders’, celebrating cinema’s ability to transcend geographical boundaries, bridge cultural differences and connect audiences through shared human emotions. Set against the backdrop of Goa’s cultural and coastal landscape, the nine-day festival aims to provide an international platform for diverse cinematic voices, creative exchange and collaboration. The inaugural ceremony featured prominent political leaders, government officials, filmmakers and artists, while international musical performances added to the celebrations. Goa aims to become a comprehensive filmmaking hub: Pramod Sawant Addressing the gathering, Goa Chief Minister Dr. Pramod Sawant said IFFI had become an integral part of the state’s cultural calendar over the past 22 years. He noted that the festival celebrates cinema’s ability to bring different cultures together and linked this year’s theme to India’s timeless philosophy of Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam — the world is one family. “Cinema allows us to experience different cultures and find the common ground that unites us,” he said. Highlighting the inclusion of Ramayana in the BRICS Cinema section, Sawant described it as a proud moment for India. He also underlined IFFI’s role in promoting Indian cinema, particularly Marathi, Konkani and Goan films, and expressed hope that the festival would encourage more young people from Goa to take up filmmaking and present their stories to national and international audiences. Outlining the state’s ambition to develop a comprehensive filmmaking ecosystem, the Chief Minister said, “We want Goa to be the destination where films are produced and completed.” He highlighted the Goa Film Shooting Act, 2021, the online single-window clearance system and financial assistance schemes for filmmakers as key measures to strengthen the state’s film industry. He also announced a vision to establish a film city equipped with pre-production and post-production facilities, visual effects (VFX) infrastructure and film education facilities. Sawant said advancements in animation, artificial intelligence and virtual production were creating new opportunities for the film industry. Goa, he added, aims to equip its young creative talent to participate in the rapidly evolving global filmmaking landscape. Truth, emotion and compelling stories connect audiences: Ravi Kishan Actor and Member of Parliament Ravi Kishan said the theme ‘Stories Without Borders’ resonated deeply with him, given his experience of working in nearly 700 films across different Indian languages and regions. He observed that audiences across linguistic and geographical boundaries connect with the same essential elements of cinema — truth, emotion and a compelling story. “A story born in one corner of the world can find a home thousands of miles away. That is the magic of cinema,” he said, describing films as a powerful medium for creating shared human experiences. Kishan also acknowledged Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s leadership in strengthening India’s film industry and noted that India is the world’s largest film-producing nation. Cinema is a powerful expression of India’s soft power: Chanchal Kumar Secretary, Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, Chanchal Kumar, described IFFI as more than a celebration of films, calling it a meeting place of cultures, ideas, memories and human experiences. Quoting the Rig Vedic thought, “Let noble thoughts come to us from all directions,” he emphasised that openness to the world enriches India’s identity. He said cinema remains one of the country’s most powerful expressions of soft power and provides an effective platform for cultural exchange. The spirit of international engagement is reflected in IFFI 2026 through special showcases from Russia and Spain, along with 21 films from BRICS nations, he noted. Kumar said a story from one part of the world could reach audiences elsewhere through emotion, imagination and shared human experiences. He also highlighted the festival’s focus on fresh voices and inclusive storytelling, with 52 women filmmakers and 62 debut filmmakers featuring in this edition. A story can cross borders without a passport: Ashutosh Gowariker IFFI Festival Director Ashutosh Gowariker reflected on cinema’s ability to bring people together at a time when greater connectivity often coexists with cultural isolation. national_raw_news.title: 57th IFFI showcases 12 Goan films, bringing Konkani and Marathi stories to global audiences
national_raw_news.content: Twelve films in Konkani and Marathi will bring the stories, people and cultural experiences of Goa to an international audience at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI), offering a cinematic exploration of the state’s social realities, traditions and everyday lives. The specially curated Goan film package, scheduled to be screened at INOX Panjim from November 21 to 28, 2026, features a mix of feature films and short films. The selection explores themes such as identity, family relationships, personal struggles, childhood, loneliness and self-discovery, presenting narratives that are rooted in local experiences but carry universal emotional appeal. From an elderly woman confronting her conscience and a forgotten local hero revisiting his past to a daughter seeking reconciliation with her family and an old villager defending his ancestral home, the films cover a wide range of human experiences. The collection also includes comedies and dramas that examine changing social relationships and the complexities of everyday life. Stories of identity, family and personal discovery Among the Konkani films, Manguirish J. Bandodkar’s 30-minute Ancessao follows an elderly woman living alone in a quiet Goan village. She fills the silence of her life by talking about others but eventually realises that her gossip is a way of avoiding her own unresolved grief. Prompted by her conscience, she resolves to change her behaviour, although the transformation proves short-lived. Vardhan Vijaykumar Kamat’s Umesh, a 99-minute Konkani film, explores identity, trust and the consequences of a forgotten legacy. It follows a once-celebrated local hero who now lives in isolation in a rural village, surviving on odd jobs and carrying the burden of an unresolved past. His circumstances change when aspiring filmmakers Anton and Rohan arrive to document his life. Their investigation into local rumours and half-truths gradually reveals his forgotten talent and the painful reasons behind his withdrawal from society. As a relationship of trust develops, Umesh becomes increasingly uncomfortable with the camera. Family ties, tradition and reconciliation form the core of Prasad M. Naik’s 11-minute film Shakuntala. The story follows a woman who becomes estranged from her conservative family after marrying a Christian man from her neighbourhood. Years later, after her father’s death, she is denied the opportunity to attend his funeral. As the twelfth-day death ritual approaches, she gathers the courage to return to her childhood home, confronting long-buried conflicts and social judgment in an effort to reclaim her place as a daughter. Shravan Kankonkar’s 25-minute Purnata takes a different approach to the continuity of life through the journey of Zayo, a garland of jasmine flowers. As the garland passes through different hands, it brings comfort, hope and happiness during moments of joy and sorrow. Even as the flowers wither, they continue to touch lives, reflecting on how purpose and life carry forward even when one journey comes to an end. Relationships, memories and the challenges of growing up Suvidha Torgal Bakhle’s 16-minute Konkani film Noise examines human behaviour and recurring patterns in relationships. Its central character, Tara, struggles to move away from a troubled relationship but repeatedly finds herself drawn towards familiar patterns despite her efforts to heal. The recurring presence of an old fan serves as a metaphor for these cycles and the difficulty of changing behaviour even when the need for change is recognised. In the Marathi film Daryaa, directed by Kishor Arjun, a 25-minute narrative explores the experience of discovering the world through imagination and senses beyond sight. The story follows Aakash, a visually impaired boy with cerebral palsy who has never seen the sea and knows it only through stories, sounds and imagination. When his grandfather takes him on an unexpected journey to the coast, Aakash encounters the place he has long dreamed of visiting. The film reflects on the meaning of seeing and the ways people experience the world. Sankalp Sainath Parab’s 14-minute Konkani film Perfect Shot follows Vasudha, a young film school student whose pursuit of the perfect cinematic frame becomes an obsession with the Golden Ratio, symmetry and the rule of thirds. At the same time, she struggles with unresolved feelings towards her late father, believing he left her with nothing of value. As memories resurface, her pursuit of visual perfection turns into a journey of...

Access the E-Library India is emerging as a global research hub for diabetes: Dr Jitendra Singh November 21, 2026 | Saturday | News Dr Jitendra Singh informed that more than a dozen research projects related to diabetes are underway image credit- pib Union Minister Dr Jitendra Singh, Ministry of Science and Technology, said that India is emerging as a global research hub for diabetes, genetic disorders, and next-generation health solutions. More than a dozen diabetes-related research projects are currently underway under the Ministry of Science and Technology, primarily through the Department of Biotechnology (DBT) and to a lesser extent CSIR. Dr Jitendra Singh was addressing the inaugural ceremony of RSSDI-2026, being held in Bengaluru from November 19-22. Leading diabetologists, clinicians, researchers, academics, and health professionals from India and abroad are participating in the conference. One of the major ongoing research initiatives is an India-Denmark collaborative study investigating India-specific alterations in the gut microbiota in prediabetic and diabetic patients. This study aims to advance understanding of the role of gut microbial patterns in metabolic disorders. Another DBT-supported study involves genetically modified E. coli Nissle 1917, capable of producing GLP-1, and has the potential to be developed as a probiotic-based approach to delivering therapeutic molecules through the digestive tract, with human studies anticipated. Research at BRIC-THSTI is also studying the expression of GLP-1 analogs in gut-associated bacteria to discover new ways to deliver GLP-1-based therapies. The Union Minister also mentioned research on interventions to reduce cardiovascular metabolic risks from conception to early childhood, including childhood blood sugar, blood pressure, and obesity, as well as the ongoing EINSTEIN study in rural Mysuru. national_raw_news.title: PM to visit West Bengal and Uttar Pradesh on 21 November | Prime Minister of India
national_raw_news.content: PM to visit West Bengal and Uttar Pradesh on 21 November | Prime Minister of India News Updates PM to visit West Bengal and Uttar Pradesh on 21 November 20 Nov, 2026 PM to participate in Platinum Jubilee celebrations of IIT Kharagpur PM to participate in the 5th Kaushal Deekshant Samaroh in Lucknow 52 national-level toppers from Industrial Training Institutes, National Skill Training Institutes and Institutes for Training of Trainers to be felicitated for outstanding achievements Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi will visit West Bengal and Uttar Pradesh on 21 November 2026. At around 9:45 AM, Prime Minister will participate in the Platinum Jubilee celebrations of IIT Kharagpur. He will also address the gathering on the occasion. After that, he will travel to Bihar to lay the foundation stone and inaugurate development projects in Vaishali. Thereafter, Prime Minister will travel to Uttar Pradesh. At around 5:30 PM, Prime Minister will participate in the 5th Kaushal Deekshant Samaroh at Indira Gandhi Pratishthan in Gomti Nagar, Lucknow. He will also address the gathering on the occasion. PM in Kharagpur Prime Minister will participate in the Platinum Jubilee celebrations of IIT Kharagpur. He will also interact with 75 students of IIT Kharagpur, symbolising the Institute’s 75-year journey. IIT Kharagpur, established in 1951, was the first Indian Institute of Technology to be set up in the country. Recognised as an Institute of National Importance, it has played a pioneering role in advancing technical education, research and innovation in India. PM in Lucknow Prime Minister will participate in the 5th Kaushal Deekshant Samaroh. Instituted in the academic session 2021-22, the Kaushal Deekshant Samaroh has emerged as an annual national platform to recognise excellence in skill development and celebrate the transition of skilled youth from training to the world of work. Since its inception, the ceremony has felicitated All India toppers and high achievers from the skill development ecosystem, fostering a culture of pride, achievement and aspiration around vocational education and skilled careers. This year, 52 national-level toppers from Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs), National Skill Training Institutes (NSTIs) and Institutes for Training of Trainers (IToTs) will be felicitated for their outstanding achievements. Top Stories of the Day Share DD India November 21, 2026 1:17 AM IST Indian Navy | Diving Support Craft | DSC A21 Indian Navy receives indigenously built diving support craft DSC A21 in Mumbai Author: DD India The Indian Navy on Friday received DSC A21, the latest vessel under its Diving Support Craft (DSC) project, at Naval Dockyard, Mumbai. The vessel has been indigenously designed and constructed by Kolkata-based Titagarh Rail Systems Limited (TRSL). Featuring a catamaran-hull design, DSC A21 is equipped with state-of-the-art diving equipment and specialised systems to support the Navy’s underwater operations. Its design provides enhanced stability, an enlarged deck area and improved sea-keeping characteristics, making it suitable for its specialised operational role. Indigenous design and construction The vessel has been designed and built indigenously in accordance with the relevant Naval Rules and Regulations of the Indian Register of Shipping (IRS). The Naval Science and Technological Laboratory (NSTL), Visakhapatnam, undertook hydrodynamic analysis and model testing during the design stage. With the induction of vessels under the project, the Indian Navy’s capabilities in diving support, underwater inspection, salvage assistance and coastal operational deployment are set to receive a boost. DSC A21 also represents the government’s Make in India initiative in the defence sector, highlighting the contribution of domestic industry to the design and construction of specialised naval platforms. Exports to Africa registered the highest growth of 44% , followed by Asia at 21%. The Americas recorded 13% growth, while Europe and CIS & Baltics registered increases of 8% and 7%, respectively. Engineering goods, electronic goods and petroleum products remained important export categories. Strong performance across diverse markets and product groups reflects the expanding reach of India’s merchandise exports across global regions. India’s Exports Strengthen Across Global Regions India’s exports recorded broad-based growth across major global regions during April–September 2026-27 , with Africa and Asia emerging as the fastest-growing regions . Exports to Asia increased 21% from US$ 85.84 billion to US$ 103.84 billion, while exports to Africa surged 44% from US$ 21.87 billion to US$ 31.42 billion. The Americas registered 13% growth to US$ 66.82 billion, followed by Europe at 8% to US$ 51.04 billion and CIS & Baltics at 7% to US$ 3.36 billion. The regional expansion was supported by demand across a diverse range of markets and export categories. Engineering goods, electronic goods, petroleum products, and chemicals featured prominently across regional export baskets. Regional Export Performance Asia: Exports Cross US$ 100 Billion, Led by China and Singapore India’s exports to Asia increased 21%, from US$ 85.84 billion to US$ 103.84 billion. Among the major export destinations: China and Singapore were the largest markets, with exports reaching US$ 11.39 billion and US$ 11.07 billion, respectively. Exports to China increased 36% , while those to Singapore more than doubled, registering 103% growth . Malaysia and Hong Kong also emerged as significant markets, with exports reaching US$ 5.58 billion and US$ 5.12 billion, respectively. Malaysia registered 83% growth , while Hong Kong recorded 37% growth . Other markets included Bangladesh at US$ 5.66 billion, Nepal at US$ 4.37 billion, Japan and Australia at around US$ 4.10 billion each, Sri Lanka at US$ 3.94 billion, South Korea at US$ 3.91 billion, Vietnam at US$ 3.83 billion and Oman at US$ 3.29 billion. At the commodity level, engineering goods remained the largest growing category at US$ 27.47 billion, registering 22% growth. This was followed by petroleum products at US$ 17.05 billion, up 28%. Electronic goods nearly doubled to US$ 10.54 billion, growing 91%, while gems and jewellery reached US$ 9.59 billion and organic and inorganic chemicals increased to US$ 6.17 billion . national_raw_news.title: India's critical mineral push securing mineral supplies through both domestic and overseas sources
national_raw_news.content: India's critical mineral push securing mineral supplies through both domestic and overseas sources: Ministry of Mines Secretary Keshav Chandra Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर India's critical mineral push securing mineral supplies through both domestic and overseas sources: Ministry of Mines Secretary Keshav Chandra ANI | Updated: Nov 21, 2026 07:46 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], November 21 (ANI): Ministry of Mines Secretary Keshav Chandra highlighted the Ministry's reform agenda to enhance the sector's global competitiveness through geological exploration, responsible mining, advanced processing, research, recycling and technology-enabled governance. Speaking at the Ministry of Mines-FICCI closed-door industry interaction, he also outlined recent auction reforms, including relaxation of minimum bidder requirements for certain minerals and automatic issuance of Letters of Intent. Responding comprehensively to the concerns raised by the industry, Chandra apprised participants of the various initiatives and measures already undertaken or under consideration by the Ministry. He addressed operational challenges relating to mineral block development. He urged the industry to actively consider extraction of critical minerals from resources such as red mud. The interaction also witnessed the launch of a concept paper, Enabling Overseas Investment in Critical Minerals: Policy, Financial and Institutional Framework for Securing India's Critical Mineral Supply Chains. Chandra emphasised that to secure mineral supplies, opportunities are being explored both at the domestic and overseas levels. He observed that the paper's emphasis on moving from MoUs to project delivery aligns with the Ministry's efforts, including KABIL's overseas engagements, and expressed interest in examining its recommendations. On overseas critical mineral investments, he discussed the importance of enabling mechanisms to improve project viability. He emphasised the Ministry's continued efforts to address industry concerns through policy and regulatory reforms, institutional coordination and targeted interventions, while encouraging industry to actively participate in strengthening India's domestic and overseas mineral supply chains. Opening the interaction, Pankaj Satija, Co-Chair, FICCI Mining Committee and Executive VP, JSW, appreciated the Ministry's reforms in exploration, mineral auctions and mine operationalisation. He highlighted growing global supply chain vulnerabilities arising from export controls, domestic value-addition requirements and processing technology restrictions, underscoring the importance of diversified and resilient mineral supply chains for India's industrial and economic security. FICCI noted that the concept paper, prepared pursuant to the mandate received from the Ministry of Mines, draws on extensive research and stakeholder consultations to identify barriers to overseas mineral investments and propose actionable solutions. The paper also presents a Country-Priority Mineral Matrix to guide strategic overseas investments and proposes a tiered framework for prioritising projects for government facilitation. It emphasises stronger institutional coordination, streamlined approvals and integration of overseas mineral investments with domestic processing and manufacturing capabilities to translate international partnerships into assured mineral supplies for India. Under the guidance of Kadam Sandeep Vasant, Joint Secretary and Head, National Critical Mineral Mission, Ministry of Mines, the paper has been authored by Arpan Gupta, Director, FICCI and Siddhant Chandra, Assistant Director, FICCI.
